Subject: MAP milestone: technical evaluation plan & next steps

Hi Eliza / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment on the primary success metrics and your internal constraints. Per our mutual action plan (MAP), I wanted to capture the technical-eval milestone we discussed and propose next steps so we can lock the target close date into your procurement calendar.

High-level milestone (proposal)
- Milestone: Technical evaluation complete (benchmarks + sign-off)
- Owner (CardioSense): Eliza (clinical data + test dataset)
- Owner (Redwood): Neha (technical run + benchmark report), Priyom (deployment/infra support)
- Success criteria (draft): model shortlist validated against clinical QA set, latency P95 <= 220ms, token cost <= $0.0012 per token for expected QPS, accuracy delta <= 2% vs baseline on labelled holdout
- Target completion: 2026-11-24 (suggested)
- Dependencies: shared test dataset, access to non-prod VPC or sample telemetry, procurement approval for 2-week dedicated infra window

I attached a short MAP draft that folds these items into the milestone timeline (redwood_MAP_draft_cardiosense_v1.pdf). Can you confirm: (1) the proposed target completion date above; (2) who will own providing the test dataset and the expected delivery date for that dataset; and (3) whether your security/compliance team needs any additional artifacts before we spin up the dedicated infra?

Next tactical step from our side: Neha will share a compact technical-eval plan with the exact benchmark slate, model shortlist, and the infra template we need. Once you confirm dataset timing we’ll schedule the infra window and a kickoff run.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving so we can hit your end-of-month decision milestone.

Best,
Aditya Rao

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Morgan <eliza.morgan@cardiosense.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical evaluation plan — benchmarks, model shortlist, infra template

Hi Eliza / team —

Following up with the technical-eval detail we discussed. I’ve summarized the plan below and attached a compact spreadsheet with the exact run matrix (cardiosense_tech-eval-plan.xlsx). If this looks good we’ll provision a 2-week dedicated infra window (non-prod) and schedule the kickoff.

Technical-eval summary (compact)
- Test dataset: CardioSense de-identified clinical export (~12k records) — expected delivery 2026-11-10
- Baseline: your existing in-house model v3.1 (we will use labeled holdout supplied by CardioSense)
- Model shortlist (candidate list to test):
  * RedCloud-7B (float16) — balanced accuracy baseline
  * OpenLM-3B-quant (int8) — low-latency quantized candidate
  * GLM-12B-optimized (mixed) — throughput/quality trade-off
  * Redwood-tiny-512 (quantized) — fast micro-batch latency check
- Benchmarks / success criteria:
  * Accuracy (primary clinical metric): delta <= 2 percentage points vs baseline on labeled holdout OR non-inferior on pre-agreed clinical thresholds
  * Latency: P95 inference latency <= 220ms for 1-token prefix at the expected QPS; P50 <= 90ms (micro-batch conditions as negotiated)
  * Cost: estimated token cost <= $0.0012 per token after batching/kv-cache for the production configuration tested
  * Stability: <1% error rate (OOMs, inference failures) across the run matrix
- Run plan / infra assumptions:
  * Dedicated 2-week infra window: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs for throughput + a 1-week optional rerun for edge cases
  * Data residency: runs performed in Redwood non-prod in us-west region; if you require VPC-hosted runs we can switch to private deployment but that will add ~3 days for network setup
- Deliverables:
  * Benchmark report (CSV + executive summary) with pass/fail per success criterion
  * Model recommendations and cost/latency trade-off table
  * Notebook with reproducer for the top-2 models

Open questions for CardioSense (please confirm):
1) Exact labeled holdout column definitions and any special scoring logic the clinical team uses (e.g., clinical thresholds vs raw probability).
2) Acceptance on proposed target completion date 2026-11-24 (we can compress to 11/19 if dataset is delivered today).
3) Preference for runs in Redwood-hosted non-prod vs CardioSense VPC (impacts scheduling).

If you confirm dataset delivery today I’ll ask infra to reserve the dedicated window starting 11/12 and schedule a 30-minute kickoff for 11/12 10:00am PT.

Thanks — Neha
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-3310
